findings.title: Rejected device is cached as tagged and bypasses the limit on retry
findings.body: tagDeviceUI inserts the device ID into localCache (SetDefault with 29-minute TTL) before calling CreateOrUpdateDevice, and does not evict the entry when that call returns ErrDeviceLimitReached. The first request for a new device over the limit is rejected in client.go, but any retry within 29 minutes hits the cache at line 83, returns nil, and Authenticate then issues an anonymous identity even though the device was never stored. This makes the device limit trivially bypassable by reloading the page.

findings.title: Limit check and insert are not atomic, so concurrent devices can exceed the limit
findings.body: CreateOrUpdateDevice performs CountDevices and then, in a separate DB session, INSERT ... ON CONFLICT. Two or more concurrent first-time devices (especially from different Grafana instances, whose local caches are per-process) can all observe count < deviceLimit and all insert, exceeding the configured limit. The limit needs to be enforced atomically (e.g. in a transaction/lock or a single conditional statement) if it is meant to be a hard cap.

findings.title: Anonymous authentication now synchronously blocks on device-tagging DB writes
findings.body: Authenticate previously tagged the device in a background goroutine with a 2-minute timeout and a detached context; it now calls TagDevice synchronously with the request context on every cache miss. This adds a COUNT query plus an INSERT/UPDATE to the authentication hot path for anonymous requests, so DB slowness directly increases (or, when the request context is cancelled, breaks) anonymous request latency/availability, and removes the panic recovery that the goroutine provided.

findings.title: updateDevice relies on RowsAffected, which can be 0 for a valid existing device on MySQL
findings.body: When the limit is reached, existing devices are admitted solely by updateDevice, which treats RowsAffected==0 as ErrDeviceLimitReached. MySQL by default reports rows actually changed (not rows matched), so an UPDATE that sets identical values (e.g. same client_ip/user_agent and an updated_at equal at the column's timestamp precision) returns 0 and a legitimately counted device is rejected as if it were new. The existing-device-at-limit path is also not covered by the new test, which only asserts rejection of a second distinct device.

findings.title: New device_limit setting is not declared in defaults/sample config or docs
findings.body: AnonymousDeviceLimit is read from [auth.anonymous] device_limit, but the PR does not add the key to conf/defaults.ini / conf/sample.ini or the configuration documentation. Operators have no discoverable way to learn the option exists, its default (0 = unlimited), or that negative values are also silently treated as unlimited by the deviceLimit > 0 check in the store.

findings.title: Frontend type says anonymousDeviceLimit may be undefined but backend always sends a number
findings.body: GrafanaConfig declares anonymousDeviceLimit as 'number | undefined' and GrafanaBootConfig defaults it to undefined, but the Go DTO (pkg/api/dtos/frontend_settings.go) is a plain int64 without omitempty, so the server always serializes it (0 when unset). Frontend code distinguishing 'not configured' (undefined) from 'configured as 0/unlimited' will never observe undefined from a real boot payload, making the two states indistinguishable.
